test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Armature and Coil Winder) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is typically done after rewinding a DC motor's armature?

options.text: The armature is immediately connected to a load for testing.
The armature is balanced and tested for performance.
The armature is coated with a protective layer.
The armature is placed directly back into the motor casing.

solution:
The correct answer is __The armature is balanced and tested for performance**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The armature of a DC motor__ is an essential component that requires proper handling after rewinding.
 
• After rewinding, the armature is balanced to ensure it operates smoothly without causing vibrations.
 
• It is also tested for performance to verify its electrical and mechanical integrity.
 
• Balancing prevents wear and tear on bearings and other motor components.
 
• Testing ensures that the rewinding process has been successfully completed and the motor can function efficiently.
 
• Skipping the balancing and testing steps may lead to operational issues or premature failure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Connecting immediately to a load without testing could result in damage.
 
• **Option 3:** Protective coating may be applied, but it is not the immediate next step.
 
• **Option 4:** Placing it back into the casing directly skips critical steps like balancing and testing.
</ul
